children: ), a global leader in cell-free DNA and precision medicine, and TransCode Therapeutics, Inc. (

), a clinical stage company pioneering immuno-oncology and RNA-based therapeutics for the treatment of high-risk and advanced cancers, today announced a strategic collaboration in colorectal cancer (CRC).

The collaboration will support enrollment for TransCode’s Phase 2a trial evaluating TTX-MC138 in patients with CRC. Patients will be eligible for enrollment if they have completed curative-intent therapy and remain positive for molecular residual disease (MRD), as detected by Natera’s Signatera test, with no radiographic evidence of disease. The collaboration aims to surface patient populations who meet the trial’s MRD-positive eligibility criteria more efficiently, streamline site-level identification, and optimize the pace and quality of enrollment for the study.

The patient population studied in the trial faces a significant risk of recurrence, yet there are currently no approved therapies for MRD-positive patients who remain disease-free on imaging. TTX-MC138 works to address this critical treatment gap by intervening earlier in the disease course.

“Identifying recurrence of colorectal cancer before it becomes clinically apparent, when it is potentially much easier to treat, is one of the central challenges in developing breakthrough therapies that help to answer unmet medical needs for this setting,” said Philippe P. Calais, PharmD, Ph.D., chairman and CEO, TransCode Therapeutics. “Leveraging one of the most established MRD testing footprints will help us identify high-risk patients faster and potentially intervene earlier, advancing a new treatment paradigm focused on addressing cancer at the molecular residual disease stage before recurrence becomes clinically apparent.”

“We are pleased to collaborate with TransCode to bring the power of Signatera to bear on one of the most difficult problems in clinical development: finding the right patients at the right time,” said Eric Matthews, general manager, biopharma, Natera. “By identifying Signatera MRD-positive patients for enrollment, we aim to support the advancement of this promising therapy for patients and build on the growing clinical and scientific momentum supporting MRD-guided strategies in colorectal cancer.”

TransCode’s study is being conducted by Quantum Leap Healthcare Collaborative within its PRE-I-SPY program, a leading platform for innovative oncology clinical trials. This trial represents the program’s first expansion beyond breast cancer into CRC. The PRE-I-SPY platform extends the clinically validated I-SPY trial model into early feasibility testing to accelerate biologically targeted therapies into the curative-intent setting. TTX-MC138 is a first-in-class therapeutic candidate designed to inhibit microRNA-10b (miR-10b), a biomarker widely linked to the emergence and progression of metastatic cancers, including CRC. More information can be found at clinicaltrials.gov (NCT05868226).

Natera is a global leader in cell-free DNA and precision medicine, dedicated to oncology, women’s health, and organ health. We aim to make personalized genetic testing and diagnostics part of the standard-of-care to protect health and inform earlier, more targeted interventions that help lead to longer, healthier lives. Natera’s tests are supported by more than 400 peer-reviewed publications that demonstrate excellent performance. Natera operates ISO 13485-certified and CAP-accredited laboratories certified under the Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA) in Austin, Texas, and San Carlos, California, and through Foresight Diagnostics, its subsidiary, operates an ISO 27001-certified and CAP-accredited laboratory certified under CLIA in Boulder, Colorado. For more information, visit www.natera.com.

TransCode Therapeutics is an immuno-oncology and targeted cancer therapy company with a focus on treating advanced malignancy. The company’s lead therapeutic candidate, TTX-MC138, is focused on treating metastatic tumors that overexpress microRNA-10b, a unique, well-documented biomarker of metastasis, and is currently being evaluated in a Phase 2a trial under the PRE-I-SPY program in collaboration with Quantum Leap Healthcare Collaborative. In addition, TransCode has a portfolio of other first-in-class therapeutic candidates designed to mobilize the immune system to recognize and destroy cancer cells. For more information, visit www.transcodetherapeutics.com.
